newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: KNP BT seen poised for recovery after poor 1996.
newsitem.headline: KNP BT seen poised for recovery after poor 1996.

text.p: Dutch paper, packaging and office products group KNP BT should post sharply lower full-year 1996 results on Wednesday but is poised for a modest turnaround this year, analysts say.

Forecasts for fourth quarter 1996 net from ordinary operations range from 62 to 107 million guilders, compared with a year-earlier 151 million. This would take full-year profits to between 202 and 245 million guilders from 545 million in 1995.
The estimates exclude extraordinary items and a 35 million guilder annual dividend to preference shareholders. In 1995, KNP BT posted an extraordinary charge of 75 million guilders.

"The bottom-line figures are not really that important ...it's what the company has to say about the current situation in the paper market and its future prospects that really counts," said Ab Barneveld, analyst with Generale Bank.
Margins at KNP BT's paper-making unit Leykam were improving, he said, but this was unlikely to have a major impact on the fourth-quarter result.
"I don't think Leykam's total result will rise above break-even," agreed ING Bank analyst Thibaud de Guerre.
He said the paper maker would have suffered from higher pulp prices that could not be immediately passed on to customers.
"But I expect paper prices to start picking up soon," De Guerre added.

Paper demand had been strong throughout the summer and this had continued into the fourth quarter, De Guerre said. High volumes would also have boosted results at KNP's distribution division, where paper merchanting is a key activity.
"I think we have seen the absolute rock-bottom in 1996, and things will start improving in 1997," De Guerre said.
Results at KNP BT's packaging division would also improve as restructuring measures started to bear fruit, he added.
Rabo Securities' Jan Wirken predicted Leykam could make a small profit in the fourth quarter, although for the full year it was set for an operating loss of some 31 million guilders.
"The huge volumes in paper could help Leykam to a fourth quarter profit, despite sustained pressure on margins," he said.
"The price of wood-free coated paper is under constant pressure," he said, but added prices were expected to gain strength in 1997.
Wirken said he had upgraded KNP BT to a "Hold" recommendation from "Sell", based on expectations that the worst was over at its paper division.
ING Barings has the stock as a "Buy", while Generale's Barneveld said he was erring on the side of caution in keeping it a "Hold".
"It is advisable to be careful," he said. "But based on current sentiment I would be more inclined to upgrade to a "Buy" than the reverse."
